findings.text: The line format, the append-only clearing, the `drop`/`clear` tools with `from` taken from the caller, the POST route, the drawer rows (newest first, from · age · Clear), the "AI · N" count and Servex/doc/inbox.md all match requirements.md. ext/drawer/inbox.js:404 hides the empty inbox with the `hidden` attribute, but the box also has the `.flex` class, and framework.css:832 `.flex { display: flex }` beats the browser's own `[hidden]` rule. So the empty box stays in the layout. It has no height, but it can add one extra gap to `.drawer-ai`. Compare drawer-1920-cleared.png with a page from before this change, or add `.drawer-inbox[hidden] { display: none; }` to drawer.css.

ext/drawer/inbox.js:361: when a drop fails, nobody is told. On a card page or query view that has no folder of its own, the route answers 404, `drop()` doesn't check `ok`, and the note the owner typed disappears without a word. Showing the `why` next to the button would fix it.

Servex/agents/inbox.js:155: the POST route takes `from` and `by` from the request body, so any caller can sign a note with any agent's name. That is fine on loopback, but doc/inbox.md should say that the name isn't checked on this path, unlike the MCP tool.

ext/drawer/tabs.js:462 and tabs/ai.js:493 both fetch `/api/inbox` every time the AI tab opens (once for the count, once for the rows). That works, but the count could come from the view's own `drawer-inbox` event when the AI tab is the one showing.
